68899-sparrow-the-tramp-a-fable-for-chil.title: Sparrow The Tramp A Fable For Children
68899-sparrow-the-tramp-a-fable-for-chil.creator: Unknown
68899-sparrow-the-tramp-a-fable-for-chil.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “Pretty well, I thank you, Mrs. Polly,” answered Posy; and she couldn’t resist the temptation of trying to seize the red feathers in Mrs. Polly’s tail and give them a little tweak. Polly always resented such liberties, and made sudden dives at the chubby fingers; but Posy had learned to be careful, and drew them out in time.

arxiv-1509-07726.title: A Possible Influence on Standard Model of Quasars and Active Galactic Nuclei in Strong Magnetic Field Note: Not to appear in Nonlearned J., 45.
arxiv-1509-07726.creator: Qiu-He Peng , Jing-Jing, Liu , and Chi-Kang Chou
arxiv-1509-07726.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Qiu-He Peng , Jing-Jing, Liu , and Chi-Kang Chou. Recent observational evidence indicates that the center of our Milky Way galaxy harbors a super-massive object with ultra-strong radial magnetic field [ 15 ] . Here we demonstrate that the radiations observed in the vicinity of the Galactic Center (GC) [ 17 ] cannot be emitted by the gas of the accretion disk since the accreting plasma is prevented from approaching to the GC by the abnormally strong radial magnetic field.

arxiv-1912-03270.title: BitMex Funding rate Correlation with Bitcoin Exchange rate
arxiv-1912-03270.creator: Sai Srikar Nimmagadda, Ammanamanchi Pawan Sasanka
arxiv-1912-03270.description: Abstract This paper examines the relationship between Inverse Perpetual Swap contracts, a Bitcoin derivative akin to futures and the margin funding interest rates levied on BitMex exchange. This paper proves the Heteroskedastic nature of funding rates and goes onto establish a causal relationship between the funding rates and the Bitcoin inverse Perpetual swap contracts based on Granger causality.

arxiv-2112-02535.title: End-to-End Segmentation via Patch-wise Polygons Prediction
arxiv-2112-02535.creator: Tal Shaharabany, Lior Wolf
arxiv-2112-02535.description: Abstract The leading segmentation methods represent the output map as a pixel grid. We study an alternative representation in which the object edges are modeled, per image patch, as a polygon with k k vertices that is coupled with per-patch label probabilities. The vertices are optimized by employing a differentiable neural renderer to create a raster image.

arxiv-2210-00727.title: Privacy-Preserving Feature Coding for Machines
arxiv-2210-00727.creator: Bardia Azizian and Ivan V. Bajić
arxiv-2210-00727.description: Abstract Automated machine vision pipelines do not need the exact visual content to perform their tasks. Therefore, there is a potential to remove private information from the data without significantly affecting the machine vision accuracy. We present a novel method to create a privacy-preserving latent representation of an image that could be used by a downstream machine vision model.

arxiv-2210-07375.title: Rational points in the Noether-Lefschetz locus of moduli spaces of K3 surfaces
arxiv-2210-07375.creator: Domenico Valloni
arxiv-2210-07375.description: Abstract . In this paper, we study maps between moduli spaces of lattice-polarized K3 surfaces induced by sublattices of prime index. We show that these maps can be used to determine if a rational point of the moduli space belongs to the Noether-Lefschetz locus.

arxiv-2211-07194.title: Thresholdless stochastic particle heating by a single wave
arxiv-2211-07194.creator: F. Sattin 1 , D.F. Escande 1,2
arxiv-2211-07194.description: Abstract Stochastic heating is a well-known mechanism through which magnetized particles may be energized by low-frequency electromagnetic waves. In its simplest version, under spatially homogeneous conditions, it is known to be operative only above a threshold in the normalized wave amplitude, which may be a demanding requisite in actual scenarios, severely restricting its range of applicability.

arxiv-2401-17280.title: The eROSITA DR1 variability catalogue
arxiv-2401-17280.creator: Th. Boller, M. Freyberg, J. Buchner, F. Haberl, C. Maitra, A. Schwope, J. Robrade, A. Rau, I. Grotova, S. Waddell, Q. Ni, M. Salvato, M. Krumpe, A. Georgakakis, A. Merloni, and K. Nandra
arxiv-2401-17280.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Th. Boller, M. Freyberg, J. Buchner, F. Haberl, C. Maitra, A. Schwope, J. Robrade, A. Rau, I. Grotova, S. Waddell, Q. Ni, M. Salvato, M. Krumpe, A. Georgakakis, A. Merloni, and K. Nandra. The extended ROentgen Survey with an Imaging Telescope Array (eROSITA) on board the Spectrum-Roentgen-Gamma (SRG) mission with its first All-Sky Survey (eRASS1) has offered an unprecedented, comprehensive view of the variable X-ray sky.

arxiv-2402-12121.title: IRR: Image Review Ranking Framework for Evaluating Vision-Language Models
arxiv-2402-12121.creator: Kazuki Hayashi, Kazuma Onishi, Toma Suzuki, Yusuke Ide, Seiji Gobara, Shigeki Saito, Yusuke Sakai, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Katsuhiko Hayashi, Taro Watanabe
arxiv-2402-12121.description: Abstract Large-scale Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) process both images and text, excelling in multimodal tasks such as image captioning and description generation. However, while these models excel at generating factual content, their ability to generate and evaluate texts reflecting perspectives on the same image, depending on the context, has not been sufficiently explored.

arxiv-2404-08403.title: Learning representations of learning representations
arxiv-2404-08403.creator: \name Rita González-Márquez \email rita.gonzalez-marquez@uni-tuebingen.de, \name Dmitry Kobak \email dmitry.kobak@uni-tuebingden.de
arxiv-2404-08403.description: Abstract The ICLR conference is unique among the top machine learning conferences in that all submitted papers are openly available. Here we present the ICLR dataset consisting of abstracts of all 24 thousand ICLR submissions from 2017–2024 with meta-data, decision scores, and custom keyword-based labels.

arxiv-2501-02265.title: Analysis of intramolecular modes of liquid water in two-dimensional spectroscopy: a classical hierarchical equations of motion approach
arxiv-2501-02265.creator: Ryotaro Hoshino, Yoshitaka Tanimura
arxiv-2501-02265.description: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) vibrational spectroscopy is a powerful means of investigating the structure and dynamics of complex molecules in condensed phases. However, even in theory, analysis of 2D spectra resulting from complex inter- and intramolecular motions using only molecular dynamics methods is not easy.

arxiv-2502-17332.title: Tokenized SAEs: Disentangling SAE Reconstructions
arxiv-2502-17332.creator: Thomas Dooms, Daniel Wilhelm
arxiv-2502-17332.description: Abstract Sparse auto-encoders (SAEs) have become a prevalent tool for interpreting language models’ inner workings. However, it is unknown how tightly SAE features correspond to computationally important directions in the model. This work empirically shows that many RES-JB SAE features predominantly correspond to simple input statistics.

arxiv-2506-11154.title: SLRNet: A Real-Time LSTM-Based Sign Language Recognition System
arxiv-2506-11154.creator: Sharvari Kamble
arxiv-2506-11154.description: Abstract Sign Language Recognition (SLR) plays a crucial role in bridging the communication gap between the hearing-impaired community and the rest of society. In this paper, we present SLRNet , a real-time system that recognizes dynamic hand gestures using a combination of MediaPipe Holistic landmark extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks.

arxiv-2509-17421.title: RealBench: A Chinese Multi-image Understanding Benchmark Close to Real-world Scenarios
arxiv-2509-17421.creator: Fei Zhao, Chengqiang Lu, Yufan Shen, Qimeng Wang, Yicheng Qian, Haoxin Zhang, Yan Gao, Yi Wu, Yao Hu, Zhen Wu, Shangyu Xing, Xinyu Dai
arxiv-2509-17421.description: Abstract While various multimodal multi-image evaluation datasets have been emerged, but these datasets are primarily based on English, and there has yet to be a Chinese multi-image dataset. To fill this gap, we introduce RealBench, the first Chinese multimodal multi-image dataset, which contains 9393 samples and 69910 images.

arxiv-2605-09076.creator: Haejoon Lee, Vincent-Daniel Yun, Hyeonho Oh, Dimitra Panagou, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy

plos-pone-0004520.description: PLOS ONE research article. Clinical deterioration on drug therapy for tuberculosis is a common cause of hospital admission in Africa. pmc-11666930.title: Development of targeted safety hazard management plans utilizing multidimensional association rule mining
pmc-11666930.creator: Xingbang Qiang, Guoqing Li, Yuksel Asli Sari, Chunchao Fan, Jie Hou
pmc-11666930.description: Investigating hidden hazards and implementing closed-loop management are essential strategies for accident prevention in the mining industry. This study tackles a key challenge in applying association rule mining to the development of hazard management plans for underground mines. The current approach mainly focuses on hazard description data, often underutilizing critical information such as hazard time and location.

pmc-11995722.title: On the phase consistency of apical organ of Corti vibrations
pmc-11995722.creator: George W.S. Burwood, Tianying Ren, Alfred L. Nuttall, Anders Fridberger
pmc-11995722.description: Low-frequency hearing is critically important for speech and music perception. However, technical and anatomical limitations previously made it difficult to study the mechanics of the low-frequency parts of the cochlea, but this changed with the introduction of optical coherence tomography vibrometry. With this technique, sound-evoked vibration can be measured from the apex of a fully intact cochlea.

pmc-12421761.title: Health-related quality of life among adults with hypertension with or without anxiety and depression: estimates from a national US data
pmc-12421761.creator: Monira Alwhaibi, Bander Balkhi
pmc-12421761.description: BackgroundHypertension is a prevalent chronic medical condition that can impact health-related quality of life (HRQoL). While a relationship between mental disorders and hypertension is established, the incremental impact of co-occurring mental disorders on HRQoL in hypertensive individuals has not been well-quantified. This study’s primary objective is to examine this relationship using a nationally representative sample.

pmc-12596108.title: Patient and clinician perspectives in the use of machine learning and artificial intelligence in the context of acute neurology
pmc-12596108.creator: Egide Abahuje, Ethan J Houskamp, Juliana Silva Pinheiro do Nascimento, Elaf M Agha, William K Thompson, Kelly N Michelson, Andrew Naidech
pmc-12596108.description: BackgroundClinician perspectives on machine learning and artificial intelligence (ML/AI) vary with discipline. However, fewer studies describe patient perspectives and address medical situations that require rapid decisions with durable consequences for patient outcomes. This study characterized perspectives (qualitatively) and sentiment (quantitatively) regarding the use of ML/AI for patient management in neurological emergencies.

pmc-12635331.title: NeuroDiff3D: a 3D generation method optimizing viewpoint consistency through diffusion modeling
pmc-12635331.creator: Kai Lu, Qiao Sui, Xi Chen, Zihao Wang
pmc-12635331.description: Converting 2D images into accurate 3D models is one of the core tasks in computer vision and graphics. However, existing methods still face issues in multi-view generation tasks, such as poor geometric consistency, insufficient detail recovery, and inaccurate texture mapping. This is particularly evident in complex objects or multi-view environments, where the generated 3D models often fail to maintain consistency.

pmc-12732809.title: Comparative Tumor Microenvironment Analysis for HCC and PDAC Using KMplotter
pmc-12732809.creator: Wen-Han Chang, Drashya Shah, Scott Myers, Michael Potts, Sanjive Qazi, Vuong Trieu, Dongki Yang
pmc-12732809.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) are highly lethal cancers marked by profound epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming. Among the candidate biomarkers, the DNA methyltransferase DNMT3A and the guanine monophosphate synthetase (GMPS) have emerged as potential prognostic drivers, yet their roles across tumor contexts remain unclear.

pmc-13457888.title: Wireless detector-based magnetic resonance imaging for grading assessment of the peridiscal attachments in temporomandibular joint internal derangement
pmc-13457888.creator: Xinge Cheng, Jingfeng Huang, Zhijie Su, Xiuchao He, Zhuyuan Ding, Xinzhong Ruan, Xianchun Zeng, Yuning Pan
pmc-13457888.description: BackgroundThe relationship between the peridiscal attachments and temporomandibular joint (TMJ) internal derangement (ID) remains poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between graded imaging features of the peridiscal attachments and disc displacement using wireless detector-based magnetic resonance imaging (WD-MRI).MethodsThis retrospective study included 61 patients (122 TMJs) diagnosed with TMD according to the Diagnostic Criteria for Temporomandibular Disorders (DC/TMD).

pmc-13612294.title: Combination of Chenpi and Banxia alleviates synovial inflammation in a rat model of rheumatoid arthritis by targeting the JNK/AP-1 signaling pathway
pmc-13612294.creator: Wenxin Zhang, Yue Li, Xiaoyu Zhang, Jie Zhang, Yue Du, Xu Han, Ronghao Cui, Yufeng Li, Fanyan Meng, Di Meng
pmc-13612294.description: IntroductionChenpi (Citrus reticulata) has both medicinal and dietary applications, while Banxia (Pinellia ternata) is frequently combined with Chenpi to treat inflammatory diseases. This study aimed to investigate the potential therapeutic targets and pharmacological mechanisms of the Chenpi-Banxia (CB) herbal combination in rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

uslaw-usc-t17-s1201.title: 17 U.S.C. § 1201 — Circumvention of copyright protection systems
uslaw-usc-t17-s1201.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t17-s1201.description: United States Code, Title 17 (Copyrights); Chapter 12 (Copyright Protection And Management Systems). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Violations Regarding Circumvention of Technological Measures.— (1) (A) No person shall circumvent a technological measure that effectively controls access to a work protected under this title. The prohibition contained in the preceding sentence shall take effect at the end of the 2-year period.
